Ecosystem Accords bind an Agent to Sky by mutual agreement r

title: Sky Governance cannot unilaterally rewrite an Ecosystem Accord: modification requires the consent of every affected party
content:
A.2.8.3.1 requires that modification, suspension, or termination of an Ecosystem Accord obtain "the mutual consent of each party to the Accord whose rights, obligations, or commercial terms are affected." A.2.8.3.1.1 defines Sky's half of that consent as Sky Governance approving the Atlas Edit Proposal incorporating the change; A.2.8.3.1.2 requires every other party to express agreement "through a channel through which Core GovOps can verify the party's agreement" — the Sky Forum (A.2.8.3.1.2.1) or a private channel established by Core GovOps (A.2.8.3.1.2.2). Core GovOps then packages the agreed change into an Atlas Edit Proposal (A.2.8.3.1.3).

This is a genuine self-limitation. The Atlas is Sky's own document and governance can otherwise edit it, but because Accord terms live inside the Atlas, an unrestricted edit power would let Sky void its commitments by amending its own text. The consent requirement converts those sections into something contract-like: still stored in the Atlas, no longer unilaterally editable.

The scoping clause matters — consent is owed only by parties "whose rights, obligations, or commercial terms are affected." This keeps one counterparty from holding up housekeeping that does not touch it.

For Primes, consent flows through the Prime Agent's authorized representative, "which acts on behalf of its affiliates, including its Foundation and Development Company" — so the three-entity party structure collapses to a single signing authority, and Sky does not have to collect three signatures.
description: Sky's consent is the Atlas Edit approval; each other party must consent through a channel Core GovOps can verify. Governance's sovereignty over its own rulebook stops at Accord terms.
